root_cause: Only simulation_timeout is reported, with empty trace_mismatches and no compile tail, so this is a global liveness/deadlock rather than a wrong-data failure. The most likely cause is an undriven or misconnected ready/stop-fetch/commit-metadata net in the rv32i5 top-level integration, or an equivalent rename/ROB/issue backpressure loop: fetch or dispatch stops permanently and no ECALL reaches commit, so halted is never asserted. The ECALL/exit_code halt path is the secondary suspect once the structural stall is ruled out.
repair_constraints: Do not rename any modules, files, or ports; preserve the exact interface contract including all debug outputs.
Keep the synchronous active-low reset semantics; dmem_valid must be 0 during reset and PC priority reset > redirect > ECALL freeze > load-use > PC+4 must be preserved.
Do not retract an issued imem/dmem request: hold valid and address until ready; halt/flush may suppress only responses and must not abort an in-flight transaction.
Preserve the ECALL/halt sequence: ECALL remains valid through ID/EX/MEM/WB, exactly one dbg_retire_valid on the commit edge, halted/exit_code=x10 on the next edge, and stable outputs while halted.
Preserve one retire event per committed instruction and no retire events for squashed, invalid, or stalled entries.
Every module output used by another module must be driven and connected at the rv32i5 top level; avoid combinational ready loops and pipeline-register overwrite without backpressure.
